gsas.name: Turner Island Water District GSA-1
gsas.note: Named in the synthesis as having no instrument in the reviewed document set; no findings are coded to it.

isw_model.detail: Quasi-3D numerical model on the IWFM 2015 platform, calibrated against ET, groundwater levels, and streamflow.

mlrp_structure.value: MSGSA holds the Department of Conservation block grant directly
mlrp_structure.detail: $8.89M DOC MLRP block grant awarded 16 June 2023 and held by MSGSA, alongside a locally funded Proposition 218 Phase 1 Land Repurposing Program.

profile.key_characteristic: The one basin that currently produces a measured water figure tied to a specific repurposing agreement, using its compliance instrument.

communities.text: Disadvantaged-community noticing is delegated to Self-Help Enterprises and Leadership Counsel; MIUGSA holds a standing disadvantaged-community advisory seat.

indicators.name: Chronic lowering of groundwater levels
indicators.why: ISW criteria are carried over from the groundwater-level indicator; a pumping-allocation rule adjusts automatically on level triggers.

indicators.name: Land subsidence
indicators.why: The July 2026 Rules tie allocation and well approval to pumping above the Corcoran Clay in subsiding zones.

basins.name: Turlock Subbasin
basins.scope_note: Findings are coded to the East Turlock GSA within the Turlock Subbasin. Where a document covers the whole Turlock Subbasin, the finding is coded at SUBBASIN level.

gsas.name: West Turlock Subbasin GSA
gsas.note: Runs no land repurposing program; the DOC grant was awarded to the Subbasin as a whole (Synthesis §2.1).

isw_model.detail: Quasi-3D finite element model on the IWFM 2015 platform — the same model class as Merced — calibrated October 1991 to September 2015.

accounting_platform.detail: ET data source is LandIQ, with CalETa for the historical baseline.

mlrp_structure.value: ETSGSA runs the program under a subbasin-wide award
mlrp_structure.detail: ETSGSA applied on behalf of both GSAs; DOC awarded the Subbasin $8.89M. Grant closes 31 March 2027.

profile.key_characteristic: Sets an ISW-specific undesirable result for each river; declared on two of three rivers in WY 2025 with no management consequence.

setting.text: West Turlock GSA covers about 60% of the subbasin and East Turlock GSA about 40%; the two wrote one GSP.

agriculture.text: Cover cropping is the largest demand-reduction activity in East Turlock by acreage — roughly 25,000 acres in WY 2025.

communities.text: Advocates' analysis of the GSP's own thresholds found 5.4% of evaluable domestic wells impacted.

indicators.name: Interconnected surface water
indicators.why: An undesirable result was declared on two of three rivers in WY 2025.

indicators.name: Chronic lowering of groundwater levels
indicators.why: 2027 interim milestones were set below minimum thresholds because long-term declines were expected to continue.

isw_model.detail: USGS-owned numerical model built on MODFLOW-OWHM v2. Produces a paired-simulation depletion estimate and mapped ISW locations, but the compliance criterion runs on shallow-well elevation readings rather than model output.

accounting_platform.value: No accounting platform identified in the reviewed documents
accounting_platform.detail: Recorded as an absence in the reviewed document set, not as a statement that none exists.

mlrp_structure.value: MLRP grant held outside the GSA
mlrp_structure.detail: The Greater Monterey County IRWM Group holds a $10M DOC grant covering the 180/400, Eastside and Langley subbasins; SVBGSA is a partner. The money buys land rather than paying for practices.

profile.key_characteristic: Has commissioned direct field measurement of stream-aquifer exchange, and pairs a disadvantaged-community board seat with a supermajority rule for fees and pumping limits.

map_profile.grantee_note: Grant held by the Greater Monterey County IRWM Group, covering the 180/400, Eastside and Langley subbasins.

agriculture.text: Essentially all pumping is from the 180-Foot principal aquifer, below the Salinas Valley Aquitard.

communities.text: Castroville Community Services District appoints the board's disadvantaged-community director, and has asked for more outreach on seawater intrusion's effects on health, water bills and home values.

indicators.name: Seawater intrusion
indicators.why: One of Castroville's four supply wells went offline in 2021 on chloride from seawater intrusion.

indicators.name: Interconnected surface water
indicators.why: An undesirable result was declared for WY 2022 and attributed to reservoir operations.

indicators.name: Degraded water quality
indicators.why: Amendment 1 tabulates about twenty constituents against drinking-water and Basin Plan standards.

basins.name: Kaweah Subbasin
basins.scope_note: Three GSAs each filed a separate GSP under one Coordination Agreement and a shared ISW technical memorandum. Mid-Kaweah reports no interconnected surface water.

isw_model.value: Kaweah Subbasin Groundwater Flow Model + Hunt analytical function
isw_model.detail: MODFLOW-OWHM v2 calibrated to groundwater elevations only; the GSAs state it is not yet calibrated for ISW depletion, so depletion is estimated with an analytical stream-depletion function.

accounting_platform.detail: Land IQ ET tracked per parcel per month, with a trading module.

mlrp_structure.value: Subbasin-level award implemented by the three GSAs
mlrp_structure.detail: $10M in MLRP funding according to a Self-Help Enterprises comment reproduced in the GSPs; three recharge-basin projects listed in the WY 2025 Annual Report.

profile.key_characteristic: The one basin that attaches a likelihood range to its depletion estimate, and the one with a water-trading market in operation.

climate.text: Rainfall differs by about seven inches a year between the western edge near Hanford and the eastern edge near Woodlake.

agriculture.text: Irrigated agriculture accounted for more than 94% of groundwater use in 2020.

communities.text: Projects and mitigation are sited at named disadvantaged communities including Seville, Okieville and Cameron Creek Colony.

indicators.name: Land subsidence
indicators.why: Subsidence is attributed mainly to the Lower Aquifer, below the Corcoran Clay, which sits outside the ISW analysis.

indicators.name: Chronic lowering of groundwater levels
indicators.why: The State Water Board's 2025 staff assessment ties overdraft to falling levels, subsidence and wells going dry.

isw_model.detail: Numerical model adapted from DWR's C2VSimFG on a monthly timestep; its authors describe it as not yet well calibrated and label its ISW conclusions provisional.

accounting_platform.detail: The GSAs selected a consultant team in late 2025 to build a subbasin water accounting system.

mlrp_structure.detail: The main repurposing-type activity is The Nature Conservancy's winter flooding of farmland for shorebird habitat and recharge.

profile.key_characteristic: Counts domestic wells above candidate thresholds; the revised thresholds cut projected impacts from 589 wells to 99.

climate.text: Annual precipitation ranges from about 17 to 27 inches, higher to the west.

agriculture.text: The Nature Conservancy's winter flooding of farmland for shorebird habitat adds an estimated 5.2 thousand acre-feet a year of net recharge.

communities.text: Revised thresholds cut the projected number of impacted domestic wells from 589 to 99.

indicators.name: Land subsidence
indicators.why: DWR surveys found the greatest land-surface declines in the Sacramento Valley near Arbuckle.

indicators.name: Interconnected surface water
indicators.why: Twelve near-stream wells carry ISW thresholds on the Sacramento River, Stony Creek and the Colusa Basin Drain.

isw_model.detail: Built from an earlier Yolo County IWFM; monthly timestep for WY 1971–2018, calibrated on Putah and Cache creeks and the Yolo Bypass.

accounting_platform.detail: The documents contain no mechanism that distributes pumping limits or costs between groups.

mlrp_structure.detail: Repurposing-type projects sit in the GSP project list, mostly led by community groups, a Tribe, districts or the County.

profile.key_characteristic: Anchors ISW thresholds to a 1971–2018 record rather than a recent drought, across five ISW Management Zones.

climate.text: WY 2023 brought about 30 inches of precipitation, 148% of the historical average.

agriculture.text: About 31,000 acres of managed wetlands are being added to the subbasin model; repurposing-type projects are led mostly by community groups, a Tribe, districts and the County.

communities.text: Agencies serving three designated disadvantaged communities hold voting seats, and the Yocha Dehe Wintun Nation is a voting member; some Dunnigan households rely on domestic wells.

indicators.name: Degraded water quality
indicators.why: Total dissolved solids carries a minimum threshold, added in response to public comment.

indicators.name: Interconnected surface water
indicators.why: Seventeen near-stream wells in five ISW Management Zones, with thresholds anchored to a 1971–2018 record.

SUBBASIN.label: Subbasin-level
SUBBASIN.description: The finding applies to the subbasin as a whole rather than to a single GSA.

NON-GSA.label: Non-GSA entity
NON-GSA.description: The finding is attributed to an organization that is not a GSA.

COMMENTER.label: Public commenter
COMMENTER.description: The finding comes from a public comment letter rather than an agency document.
